title: Patenting Quantum Computing Innovations – Part 4: Entanglement Swapping - Quantum Computing Report
gist: A patent-law analysis of how a quantum repeater using entanglement swapping could be rejected as an abstract idea or natural law, and how claims can be drafted around concrete repeater hardware and QKD or teleportation elements to improve eligibility. The text is bylined Sinan Utku (Covington and Burling), while the raw author field lists Doug Finke.

insights.claim: Entanglement swapping makes two particles that have never interacted become entangled, by performing a Bell-state measurement on one particle from each of two independent entangled pairs, which projects the two unmeasured particles into an entangled state.
insights.speaker: Doug Finke
insights.so_what: Core primitive for extending entanglement; the thing quantum networking patents will claim.

insights.claim: Entanglement swapping extends entanglement over larger distances by linking shorter entangled segments, but it does not itself transmit information; it must be combined with classical communication and protocols like teleportation or quantum key distribution.
insights.speaker: Doug Finke
insights.so_what: Value accrues to full-stack network systems rather than the swapping step alone.
insights.locator: This technique enables entanglement to be extended

insights.claim: Entanglement swapping forms the basis for quantum repeaters, which are expected to play a central role in future quantum communication networks.
insights.speaker: Doug Finke
insights.so_what: Quantum repeaters are a key enabling hardware segment to watch for quantum networking.
insights.locator: This technique enables entanglement to be extended

insights.claim: A repeater claim covering entanglement swapping would store one qubit of each of two entangled pairs at two nodes, run a Bell-state measurement at an intermediate node, and classically send the result to one of the end nodes.
insights.speaker: Doug Finke
insights.so_what: Shows the typical claim structure a patent drafter would use for repeater inventions.
insights.locator: A quantum repeater system that includes entanglement swapping

insights.claim: A quantum repeater invention using entanglement swapping could be challenged as patent-ineligible because an examiner or court may view it as directed to a natural law, given the centrality of the Bell-state measurement.
insights.speaker: Doug Finke
insights.so_what: Eligibility risk can weaken patent portfolios of quantum networking companies.
insights.locator: The eligibility of such an invention could be challenged

insights.claim: An examiner could argue that a Bell-state measurement implements a well-established physical process and that the invention merely projects a quantum system into entangled states without a specific, technically inventive implementation or improvement in apparatus or protocol.
insights.speaker: Doug Finke
insights.so_what: Claims lacking concrete implementation detail are most exposed to abstractness rejections.

insights.claim: Granting a patent on this invention could be criticised for preempting all practical uses of Bell-state measurements in quantum communications.
insights.speaker: Doug Finke
insights.so_what: Preemption concerns could limit how broadly early quantum networking claims are allowed.
insights.locator: might also underscore the risk of preemption

insights.claim: Eligibility could also be challenged as abstract because courts have found inventions abstract when they amount to manipulating, transmitting or correlating information, and classical channel communication may be seen as conventional and routine.
insights.speaker: Doug Finke
insights.so_what: Cites Electric Power Group v. Alstom (Fed. Cir. 2016) as the precedent underlying abstract-idea risk for quantum information claims.

insights.claim: Courts held ineligible in Electric Power Group v. Alstom an invention directed to merely collecting information, analyzing it, and displaying results.
insights.speaker: Doug Finke
insights.so_what: Precedent that patent counsel will invoke against information-processing quantum claims.
insights.quote: collecting information, analyzing it, and displaying certain results of the collection and analysis

insights.claim: Applicants can argue the quantum repeater embodies specific hardware-based improvements to a communication system by extending the effective transmission range of entanglement that quantum communication protocols rely on.
insights.speaker: Doug Finke
insights.so_what: Framing claims as network improvements is the recommended defence for quantum networking IP.
insights.locator: The applicant, on the other hand

insights.claim: Eligibility odds increase when claims specify hardware elements for the communication protocol used with the repeater, such as those implementing quantum teleportation or quantum key distribution.
insights.speaker: Doug Finke
insights.so_what: Quantum networking patents tied to concrete QKD or teleportation hardware are likely more defensible; weigh portfolios accordingly.
insights.locator: The odds of a finding of patent eligibility

insights.claim: Focusing claims on structural and operational improvements to repeater hardware and network infrastructure may help show a patent-eligible technological advance rather than an abstract idea or natural law.
insights.speaker: Doug Finke
insights.so_what: Hardware-centric claim strategy is a quality signal when assessing quantum networking patent moats.
insights.locator: Focusing on structural and operational improvements
